title: SLO-driven connection broker: opportunistic-quorum reads & soft-commit failover strategy
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
We need a new connection broker layer that enforces per-request SLO budgets and provides two resilience patterns not currently available in the runtime: (1) opportunistic-quorum reads (merge/approximate-read mode when full read quorum is unavailable) and (2) soft-commit failover for writes (accept lower durability for lower-tier SLOs rather than blocking or returning error). The broker will sit between the request router and backend connection pools (Redis/Kafka/SQL replicas) and make per-request routing + degradation decisions based on remaining SLO budget, backend health, and tenant policy.

Problem statement:
- During multi-region disruptions or replica lag spikes, strict quorum semantics cause high tail latency and request errors for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Current fallback is coarse-grained: either full degrade to cache or a full model downgrade. We lack a flexible, per-request policy that can return best-effort results while preserving correctness guarantees for higher-SLO traffic.
- Connection pools can exhaust and block under bursty load; we need admission + graceful trimming that reflects SLO tier.

Proposal:
1) Connection Broker responsibilities:
   - Maintain per-backend health score (latency, error rate, replica staleness heuristics).
   - Track per-request SLO budget (deadline remaining) and tenant tier.
   - Choose routing mode from: quorum-read, opportunistic-quorum, cached-stale-read, or soft-fail (error).
   - For writes, select commit mode: sync-primary, soft-commit (ACK after local apply), or deferred-commit (background replication).
   - Enforce per-tenant admission using token buckets with proportional trimming when pool pressure detected.

2) Opportunistic-quorum read semantics:
   - If full quorum cannot be achieved within SLO budget, attempt to read from a fastest subset of replicas and return merged result with a freshness score metadata header.
   - Attach confidence metadata so clients can make downstream decisions (e.g., revalidate, show stale indicator).
   - Automatic shadowing: duplicate a subset of requests to cold replicas during warm-up to reduce future opportunistic misses.

3) Soft-commit writes:
   - For P2/P3 SLO tiers, optionally accept a write after local durable apply (soft-commit) and return 202 with replication status available via status endpoint.
   - For P0/P1 traffic, prefer sync-primary and block until replication ack if required by tenant policy.
   - Soft-commit mode includes a small trace header to indicate when the write is still replicating so Console and audits can surface in case of inconsistency.

Design notes and engineering tasks:
- Broker will be a small stateful service colocated with the router (same pod/VM) to make decisions with low overhead.
- Introduce a new health scoring pipeline that consumes metrics (latency histograms, replica log gaps, error rates) from Console metrics API.
- Extend connection pool to expose a fast admission hook: tryReserve(timeout) -> boolean + reservation ID. The broker uses reservations to enforce proportional admission.
- Implement opportunistic merge rules per backend type: Redis: best-effort key-level reconciliation (last-write-wins with timestamp), SQL: read-from-replica with AS OF SYSTEM TIME equivalent, Kafka: read from leader with truncated tail when necessary.
- Add SDK and HTTP header changes: X-Redwood-Result-Confidence, X-Redwood-Write-Mode, X-Redwood-Replica-Age-ms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Consistency vs availability: soft-commit and opportunistic reads trade strict consistency for availability and latency. We mitigate by requiring tenant opt-in and surfacing clear metadata.
- Complexity: Broker adds a decision surface that must be tested extensively. We keep initial scope minimal (read/write modes + admission) and iterate.
- Observability burden: We add rich metadata and tracing to make incidents debuggable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Broker accepts 95th percentile router calls with <0.5ms added median overhead in canary region.
- Under simulated replica lag (500ms), opportunistic-quorum reduces tail error rate by >= 80% for P2 traffic compared to strict quorum.
- Soft-commit writes for P2 return success under replication delay scenarios and show replication-progress metrics in Console within 60s.
- New admission logic prevents connection pool exhaustion in stress test: connection reservation rejection rate <1% while maintaining SLOs for P0 lanes.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for decision logic + merge heuristics with deterministic replica-state simulators.
- Integration tests using chaos rig to introduce region partitions, replica lags, and connection pool saturation.
- Load tests that compare current behavior vs broker behavior for mixed SLO traffic patterns.
- Security and compliance review for soft-commit metadata and auditability (audit trail for lower durability writes).

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated by tenant and by route. Start with internal tenants and dev regions.
- Phase 1: Read-only opportunistic-quorum for P2/P3 routes (2-week canary in us-west-2).
- Phase 2: Add soft-commit write mode as opt-in for non-financial tenants (1 month canary).
- Phase 3: Gradual expansion with dashboards and customer opt-in flows.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Opportunistic+Quorum+and+Soft+Commit+Design
- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OpQBrokerRFC/edit
- Initial PR (work-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4897
- Canaries/dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/ops/broker-canary

Open questions / next steps:
- Decide default behavior for cross-tenant read mixing when opportunistic reads use nearby replicas that are out-of-date.
- Finalize SDK header surface for confidence metadata and client-side helpers for revalidation.
- Work with Compliance to determine retention and auditability requirements for soft-committed writes.

Notes:
- I ran a quick tabletop with infra and platform yesterday; infra suggested colocating broker to reduce hop latency. Platform raised strong concerns about making soft-commit visible in billing and audit UIs.
- Diego will spin up the health scoring prototype this week (ENG-782345-branch) and open the integration PR.

Opportunistic reads reduce tail error rate by >=80% under simulated replica lag for P2 traffic
Soft-commit writes surface replication progress in Console within 60s
Admission reservations prevent pool exhaustion under stress (reservation rejection <1%)
